title: AJ Dybantsa's Preseason Debut: 3 Key Takeaways For Wizards After Their 111-109 Win Over Knicks - NewsBreak
text:
By Chaitanya Dadhwal ,
20 minutes ago The Washington Wizards’ 2026 first-overall pick , AJ Dybantsa , got off to a promising start in his NBA career as the team defeated the New York Knicks , 111-109, in their preseason opener.
He had 11 points, two rebounds, two assists, and four steals in his preseason debut while shooting 5-for-11 from the field (45.5% FG). Here are the three key takeaways for the Wizards from Dybantsa’s first preseason game in their jersey.
1. AJ Dybantsa Shuts Down Defensive Critics Coming into the season, the first overall pick AJ Dybantsa was seen as a scoring phenom with elite athleticism who would need to work on his defense.
But his preseason performance against the fully healthy defending champions has eased criticism of his lack of effort. AJ Dybantsa recorded four steals, which especially impressed Wizards head coach Brian Keefe, who spoke about it after the game.

“The biggest thing is he had four steals. His effort on the defensive end, cutting people off, playing in the passing lane … You could feel his presence on the court, his ability to get into bodies, his ability to guard one-on-one,” the head coach said .
So the biggest takeaway from this preseason is that Dybantsa’s active hands can be a defensive asset for the Wizards.
2. AJ Dybantsa Tried To Maximize Use Of Elite Athleticism The first overall pick tried to attack the basket on multiple occasions, blowing past his defenders with elite athleticism. His pace often made the defense overcommit, but it also gave him space to take tough fadeaway shots.
His drive-ins and kick-outs against a collapsing defense show another area for potential in offensive growth for the Wizards star. If he combines his athleticism with his defense, he could help fill gaps in their defensive strategy that come with having a smaller guard like Trae Young run their offense.
3. First Look At Wizards’ Big Three Additionally, AJ Dybantsa’s preseason debut provided an early look at how he might work with Anthony Davis and Trae Young, as this was the first time the trio played together. Young’s playmaking may give the rookie more opportunities to score, letting him exploit mismatches and use his athleticism to attack the rim.
Davis can support Dybantsa on both ends of the court in the meantime. While his rim protection and defensive versatility will help cover for AJ Dybantsa’s mistakes as he adjusts to the NBA, his interior scoring and ability to draw defensive attention unlock several open driving lanes for the rookie.
Young’s playmaking vision, Davis’ two-way impact, and Dybantsa’s scoring potential give the Wizards a solid foundation to build on. But it all depends on how Dybantsa’s game develops over the season.
Now it’s a matter of how patient the Wizards’ front office is in letting this trio build chemistry for the future amid lingering concerns about Anthony Davis’ future. It remains to be seen whether this big three is their long-term solution.
